description: [S7.9, kind `measure`] cov_a_keys, cov_a_keys2, cov_a_career, cov_b_career and course_season_6y took the live core's stuck (inflated) delivery on b3d61e41 (S7.8: 1, 1, 1, 1, 6) and take none on bbc9072f / 78ffb06d (I7 inflated_compare.log; S7.9 9_inflated_probe_x64.log: cov_a_keys 0). Which commit between b3d61e41 and bbc9072f moved those dispatches to a plain call is not determined. The test now judges the mechanism on ui_tour / ui_tour_v (4 each, unchanged since S7.8).

description: [S7.9, kind `measure`] tick.cpp's HeadlessTerrain keeps its blocks (the 16 MB operator-new arena, the 1.4 MB Terrain object block of segment images, the list sentinel) in a process-wide std::map keyed by the Ctx address, and nothing erased an entry when its context was freed. A context the heap put at an address with no entry made a new one, so one Win32 runner over the 70 equivalence scenarios kept 16 MB per such context (I7: about 48 MB per scenario = boot, live and replay runs, dead near 1,765 MB); whether a run added one depended on the build's heap layout (I7's run_leak_probe.log: the boot runs in one build, the live runs in the other).
path to resolution: Resolved by roadmap S7.9: ~sg_ctx() calls the new portsim::release_headless_terrain(ctx) (tick.h), which erases the entry; a context reusing an address re-zeroed and re-mapped the entry's blocks anyway, so no run changes (segments 205 / 205 and equivalence unchanged). Measured on one runner: cov_r_bio 4 boot + 4 live runs 4 MB throughout (control, the release taken out: 20 MB from the first run); eight scenarios 4-5 MB throughout (control: 52 -> 117 MB). The app (port/app/main.cpp) creates its Ctx directly, one per session, and does not call it.

description: [S7.9, kind `measure`] cov_r_s2_screens: the live run inflates 4 dispatches (frame records 318, 342, 366, 515 by bisection) and the replay of its recording delivers 5 at another cursor count than recorded (two at record 318, then 342, 366, 515); frame records equal and PASS against the capture. The fifth is a delivery with more cursor reads than recorded (TraceInput counts both kinds as misaligned, tick.cpp batch); which dispatch it is and whether its pass differs from the live run's is not determined, so the stuck test does not use this scenario.
path to resolution: log the replay's per-dispatch call positions at record 318 (SG_TICK_INPUT_LOG lists only frames whose reads differ) against the live run's

description: [S7.9, kind `measure`] With the gfx backend attached the live core's recording of ui_tour is not the same bytes as without it (sha256 e14437e7... against 12a61999..., same length class); both replay to their own live run's frame records and drawing calls (9_stuck_probe logs, the stuck_draws run). What the backend changes in the recording (a cursor read made by a gfx body, a clock read) is not measured. The app records with the backend attached, and S7.5 / S7.8's app tests replay those recordings equal.
path to resolution: diff the two recordings with re/tools/trace_tool.py dump and name the first differing record

description: [S7.9, kind `method`] The Win32 runner serves neither sg_live_stats_ext (inflated / idle-decline counts) nor sg_run_frames_detail, so the stuck test's count check runs on x64 only; on Win32 the judge is that its live recording equals x64's byte for byte (test_stuck_recording_backends_identical).
path to resolution: serve the two calls through runner32 ops if a Win32-only defect ever needs them

description: [S7.9, kind `method`] With the gfx refresh hook (U-1670) the app presents at every Window::refreshFull. Two refreshes with no clock read between them are two presents at one recording position (the live core's LiveMarker position is the count of clock records written), and gfx.snapshotAt resolves one clock ordinal, so a replay shows only the last. Measured: every app session makes one such pair, at boot: showTitleScreen's refresh (present 0) and the first loading screen's (present 1, both position 2; 9_present0_probe2.log). The original presents both. test_app_live / test_app_ingame judge the last present at each position and require the shared ones to be exactly present 0.
path to resolution: a snapshot keyed by refresh count instead of clock ordinal (gfx.cpp) would pin present 0 too
